transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Owen. Could I get your account number to pull up your account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Owen, sure, it's 719-345-882. This is Derek Voss.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks Derek, I've got your account pulled up here. What can I help you with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My SentryCam system, the whole thing, three cameras and the hub, keeps going offline randomly. I'm missing alerts, sometimes for hours at a time, and I only find out when I check the app myself.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Got it, so all three cameras and the hub are dropping offline intermittently, and you're missing alerts during those windows without any warning. That's the kind of thing you really want reliable for a security system.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exactly, that's the whole point of having it. If it's not catching things reliably, it's not doing its job.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's been about a week now, started pretty suddenly out of nowhere.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, about a week, good to know. And does it seem to happen more at a certain time of day, or is it totally random?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pretty random honestly, sometimes in the morning, sometimes late at night.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Totally fair, let's get this addressed properly for you. Let me pinpoint what's happening on our end here, give me one second.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, I don't see an outage flagged on our side. Let's start with a reboot of the camera hub, that usually clears up connectivity issues like this.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, how long is that going to take?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It shouldn't take too long.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Alright, unplugging the hub now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Unplugged, waiting for it to come back up.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, it's back online, all three cameras showing connected again in the app.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good, let's give it a bit and see if it holds this time.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, I'll keep an eye on it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While we wait on that, has anything changed with your home network recently, any new devices, router changes, anything like that?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Actually yeah, I changed my WiFi password last week. Got a notice that my old one had been the default for way too long, so I finally updated it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's actually a really important detail, thank you for mentioning that. When exactly did the offline issues start relative to that password change?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I think it was the next day, so pretty much right after.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That timing lines up closely, that's a strong lead. Real quick, how many cameras total are connected to the hub, just so I have the full picture?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Three, like I said, two outdoor and one on the front porch.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Got it, thank you. And when you say two outdoor, are those both on the same side of the house, or opposite sides?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opposite sides actually, one covers the driveway, the other covers the backyard.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Got it, and just to confirm, both of those have been installed for a while now, nothing newly added recently?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Both been up for about a year now, nothing new there.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, that's useful, that means they're likely at different distances from the router too, which is worth keeping in mind.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Got it, thank you. And is the hub itself connected by ethernet to your router, or is it on WiFi too?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's on WiFi, same as the cameras.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, that's useful. And when you changed the password, did you update it on the SentryCam app itself, or just on the router?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Just on the router, honestly I didn't even think about needing to update it anywhere else.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, that's a really useful detail, let's keep digging a bit before I jump to conclusions though. Do all three cameras drop at the exact same time, or does it seem more staggered, like one goes down, then another a bit later?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Now that you mention it, it does seem staggered, not all at once. Sometimes it's just the front porch one, sometimes it's two of them.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a helpful distinction, a simultaneous full outage usually points to the hub itself, but staggered drops across different cameras points more toward something with the connection each camera maintains individually. Are any of the cameras battery powered, or are they all wired for power?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The two outdoor ones are battery powered, the porch one is wired.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, sorry, now that I think about it, actually the porch one might have gone down too a couple times.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's alright, good to know all three are capable of dropping rather than it being isolated to just the battery-powered ones, that helps rule out a battery-drain explanation. Can you check the signal strength shown for each camera in the app right now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me look... porch camera shows strong, the two outdoor ones show medium.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, and just to double check, is that medium reading consistent for both outdoor cameras, or does one look noticeably weaker than the other?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pretty consistent actually, both show the same two-bar medium reading.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good to know, consistent medium across both suggests it's more about distance from the router than a problem specific to one camera.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, medium signal on the outdoor two isn't unusual just from being further from the router, and since even the strong-signal porch camera has dropped too, I don't think weak signal alone explains this. Has there been any construction, new furniture, or anything metal added between the router and the cameras recently?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, nothing like that, the house layout's been the same for years.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, good, and just one more on this, is the router in the same spot it's always been, nothing moved or blocked recently?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Same spot, nothing in front of it, same as always.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, that rules that out too. One more thing, does the hub itself have any kind of event log or history you can see in the app, something that might show exactly when each drop happened?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There's a 'Device History' tab, let me check... yeah, it's showing a bunch of 'Reconnected' events, one for each camera, spread out over the last several days.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you tell roughly how many reconnect events there are total, just a rough count?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Looks like somewhere around a dozen or so across all three over the week.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a meaningful number, a dozen reconnects in a week for what should normally be a handful at most really supports the credentials theory.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's actually really useful, repeated reconnect events rather than a single continuous outage strongly suggests each device is losing its session and having to reauthenticate over and over, rather than a hardware failure or a true outage. That pattern is very consistent with a credentials mismatch rather than anything physical.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, that makes sense when you put it that way.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's check one more thing to be thorough, has your internet plan or router itself changed recently, not just the password, but the actual router or modem hardware?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, same router, just the password update I mentioned.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good, that keeps things simple, it really does point back to that password change as the trigger. I think that's actually really common, and I believe that's very likely our root cause here. The camera hub caches your WiFi credentials internally, so if the router's password changed but the hub was never told about it, it'll keep trying to reconnect with the old password, succeed for a little while on a cached session, and then drop off once that session expires, which would explain the random, intermittent pattern instead of a total outage.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, that actually makes a lot of sense, it has been kind of random rather than constantly down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly that pattern fits. Let's go ahead and re-pair the hub with the new password directly so it's not relying on a stale cached session anymore.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, how do I do that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open the SentryCam app, go to hub settings, and there should be an option that says 'Update Network'. Do you see that?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me look... yeah, found it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Tap that, and it'll ask you to select your network and enter the password again, go ahead and enter the new one.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, entering it now... done, it says connecting.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, it's showing connected now, and all three cameras just came back green in the app too.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a great sign, that means the hub successfully picked up the fresh credentials and pushed the update down to the cameras. Let's confirm it's stable, can you check your alert history and see if anything's come through in the last few minutes?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, actually, motion was just detected on the front porch camera and I got the push notification right away.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, that's exactly what we want to see, alerts coming through in real time again.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's a relief honestly, I was starting to think I'd need to replace the whole system.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Glad we caught it before that, this was really just a credentials mismatch rather than a hardware problem.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How long would you recommend I keep an eye on it before considering it fully resolved?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'd say give it through the rest of today and maybe tomorrow, if all three stay connected and alerts keep coming through normally, you're in good shape.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'll check back in throughout the day just to be safe.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a good approach, and again, if anything does come up, the notes on the account will make it a quick fix for whoever you reach.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Appreciate that.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That makes sense. Is there anything I need to do differently going forward, like if I change the password again down the line?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good question, anytime you update your WiFi password, just remember to also update it in the SentryCam app under hub settings so the hub doesn't fall out of sync again like this.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Got it, I'll remember that for next time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'll also add a note to your account documenting this fix, so if it ever comes up again, whoever you reach will have the context immediately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's great, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Out of curiosity, is there a way for the system to warn me automatically if a camera drops offline, instead of me having to notice it myself?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: There is actually, under notification settings there's a toggle called 'Device Offline Alerts', it's off by default for some reason. Want me to walk you through enabling it?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, please, that would've saved me a lot of worry this week.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Go to the app's main settings, then Notifications, then you should see 'Device Offline Alerts' near the bottom.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Found it, turning it on now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, it's on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great, now if any device drops for more than a couple minutes, you'll get a push notification immediately instead of finding out later.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's really helpful, I wish I'd known that setting existed when I first set this up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's a pretty buried setting, you're definitely not the first person to have missed it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know it's not just me. Since the porch camera is wired and the other two are battery, does the battery drain faster when they're constantly trying to reconnect like this?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Actually yes, that's a great question, repeated reconnect attempts do use noticeably more battery than a stable connection, so this issue may have also been quietly draining your two outdoor cameras faster than normal this past week.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, that would explain why I had to charge one of them a lot sooner than I expected.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That lines up, now that the hub is back on a stable, correctly authenticated connection, battery drain on those two should return to normal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know, I was starting to think the battery itself was just going bad.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Nope, should be totally fine now. Do you want me to check the current battery percentage on both while I have you, just so you have a baseline?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, that'd be helpful.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Give me a moment to pull that up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looks like 61 percent and 74 percent on the two outdoor cameras, nothing alarming, just worth keeping an eye on over the next week to confirm drain slows back down.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'll check back in on that myself in a few days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: While I've got you, is there a limit to how many cameras I can add to one hub?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: For your hub model, it supports up to six cameras total, so you'd have room to add three more if you ever wanted to expand.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know, I've actually been thinking about adding one for the backyard.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you do, just make sure it's paired while the hub is on the current, correct password, and it should be a smooth setup.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will do, appreciate the tip.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: One more thing, does the app store footage locally or in the cloud? I've always wondered.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It depends on your plan, but by default it's cloud storage with a seven day rolling history, unless you've added a local storage card to the hub.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ah, I don't think I have the local card, so it must just be cloud then.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That would track, and that's a perfectly fine default for most households.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know. Can I share access to the cameras with my wife, or does she need her own separate account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can actually invite her as a secondary user right from the app, under Household Members, she'd get her own login but see the same cameras and alerts you do.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh perfect, I've been meaning to set that up, I just never got around to finding the setting.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's under the main settings menu, should be pretty straightforward, just her email address and she'll get an invite.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, I'll do that after this call. Does she get her own notification toggles, or does it copy mine?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Her own, actually, each household member can customize their own alert preferences independently.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good, she probably doesn't want every single motion alert like I do.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's exactly the kind of thing that setup handles well then.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: One more, does the porch camera have two-way audio? I feel like I've seen that mentioned somewhere.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, actually, if you tap the camera feed there should be a microphone icon, holding that down lets you talk through the camera's speaker.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh nice, I had no idea, that could be handy for package deliveries.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly the kind of use case it's built for, works well for that.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Last one, I promise, is there a way to check the camera firmware version, just so I know it's current after all this?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Sure, under each camera's individual settings there's a 'Device Info' section that lists the firmware version and whether an update is pending.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me check... all three say up to date, good.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, that's one less thing to worry about.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Going back to what you mentioned earlier about medium signal on the outdoor cameras, is that something I should be worried about long term, even outside of this whole password issue?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's not urgent, but if you ever want to strengthen it, a mesh extender placed roughly halfway between the router and the back of the house would bring both outdoor cameras up to a stronger signal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is that something you all sell, or would I need to buy that separately?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We do offer a compatible mesh extender as an add-on, or you're welcome to use a third-party one, either works fine with the system.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know, I might look into that at some point, not urgent though since things are working now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Totally reasonable, no rush on that one, medium signal is still perfectly functional, it would just be a nice-to-have improvement.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Makes sense. Since this was on your end essentially, is there any kind of credit for the week it wasn't working properly?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a fair question, let me check what's available given the circumstances.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can apply a service credit for the affected period, I'll go ahead and put that through now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's appreciated, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course, happy to make that right given the circumstances here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: One last thing, you mentioned the seven day rolling cloud storage earlier, is there an option to extend that if I wanted a longer history?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, there's a thirty day extended history add-on available if you ever want more than the default week of footage retained.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know, I'll think about whether I actually need that or if a week is enough for my purposes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Totally your call, a week is plenty for most households unless you're trying to keep a longer archive for some specific reason.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fair enough. Would it be worth scheduling a quick follow-up call in a week or so, just to confirm everything's still holding steady?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's not something we'd normally schedule proactively, but you're always welcome to call back in if anything comes up, and like I mentioned, the notes on your account will make that quick for whoever you reach.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fair enough, that works for me too.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there a best time of day to reach support if I did need to call back, or is it the same wait either way?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Mid-morning on weekdays tends to be quieter, but we're staffed throughout the day so any time should get you through reasonably quickly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know, I'll keep that in mind.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Also, is my email on file the best way to reach me if there's ever a known outage in my area, or do you use text messages too?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We can do either, actually, would you like me to check which one is currently set as your preferred contact method?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looks like email is currently set as preferred, text isn't enabled yet.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, I'd actually prefer text for anything urgent like an outage, email I don't check as often.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No problem, I can enable text notifications for outage alerts specifically right now if you'd like.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, please, that'd be great.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Done, text alerts for area outages are now enabled on your account in addition to email.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Perfect, thank you for catching that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course, glad it came up.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fair enough. I think that answers everything on my end for now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before I let you go, just to make sure I've logged this properly, how many cameras did you say were on the account again?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Three, like I mentioned earlier, two outdoor and the front porch one.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, sorry, got that noted now, three cameras.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No worries. I think that's everything, thank you Owen.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course, glad we got that sorted out for you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Actually wait, one more thing, should I be worried this could happen again with a firmware update or something similar down the line?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's possible with any network change, but now that you know to update the password in the app whenever it changes on the router, that specific cause shouldn't repeat. Firmware updates are usually handled automatically and wouldn't cause this same issue.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, that's reassuring, thank you for explaining that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Anytime. Anything else I can help you with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, I think that covers it, thanks again Owen.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you so much, Derek. We do value your feedback, so please stay on the line after this call for a short survey. Thank you for choosing S-Net, have a great rest of your day.
